answer: A new identity starts at one inlet and must finish a voyage through three independent harbors in fixed order, each stamping it only after it clears that harbor's local backlog, work that cannot be exported or done for another clone. Each stamp expires if the next harbor is missed, so a clone cannot be parked. A summit council of unrelated reviewers checks the whole stamp chain and rejects any reused stamp. One operator running n clones faces n separate trips, n harbor queues, and clashing expiries, so delay and lost work grow faster than n, while one honest agent sails once.
